entry_item.definition: [S. nirvana] n. Nirvana (the final goal of Buddhism as opposed to reincarnation in the phenomenal world; the "absolute."

example.definition: To enter nirvana, die (esp. referring to the Buddha and saintly or exalted persons
To pass into nirvana, pass away (hon. ).

entry_item.definition: T. zhi ba; S. nirvana. Nirvana; calm.

example.definition: T. zhi mthar byed. Destroyer of nirvana's calm; the lord of the simuns.
T. zhi ba tshol ba. Seeking the (quiescent) nirvana, as the bradikabud.
T. mi gnas pahi mya ngan las hdas pa; S. apratishthita-nirvana. The nirvana which is not permanently fixed, a nirvana in which the tegyncilen iregsen returns to worldly life to save amitan. ED 48 a.

T. phung po lhag pa med pahi mya ngan las hdas pa; S. nirupadhicesha-nirvana. Nirvana without a remainder (of the five coγca). Note: nirupadhicesha, not upadhicesha. upadhi = skandlh, M. coγca. See ED 300 a. Contrasted with next term.
T. phung po lhag ma dang bcas pahi mya ngan las hdas pa; S. sopadhicesa-nirvana ( i. e. with tle five coγca somehow preserved).

entry_item.definition: affranchissement de l'âme de la douleur; annihilation; extinction de toute douleur; repos de l'âme; apathie, imperturbalitê, absorption complète dans la Raison.

example.definition: destructeur du nirvâna: chef des chimnous

entry_item.definition: der Austritt aus dem Geburtswechsel, die höchste Glückseligkeit in der Vereinigung mit der absoluten Urintelligenz, das Sanskr. Nirwâna.
(Buddhism) The dying out in the heart of the threefold fires of passion, hatred and delusion. Nirvana. A beatific spiritual condition and freedom from further transmigration.
〔名〕〈宗〉涅榮，圆寂：~ыг эзлэгч 涅榮；~ дүр нөгцөх 涅榮.

шашин. нирвана; уничтожение, освобождение духа от бремени плоти, полное успокоение, покой; нярваан дүр үзүүлэх / нярваанаа ажрах переходить к спокойствию, отойти в нирвану, умирать; нярваан болох / нярваанд нөгчих перейти в нирвану, умереть; нярвааны мөр / тонилохуйн мөр путь к нирване; нярвааны хутаг олох обрести святость нирваны, умереть.
